conviction_note: Guidance-implied Q4 FY26 adjusted EBITDA of $14.7-19.7M against a Q3 actual of $30.5M is arithmetically implausible and nobody has published it, so a large FY26 beat is likely and un-modelled (+5); against that, Colorado's enacted Medicaid rate cuts bite in FY27 (-2.5) and an 83%-of-shares resale shelf went effective five weeks ago with no announcement (-1.2), and this name's own FY-end print last year fell 2.81% on a beat because the forward guide dominated, so I net down to +2.0 with wide uncertainty and no option chain to check myself against.

findings.finding: InnovAge's raised FY2026 guidance implies a Q4 adjusted EBITDA of only $14.7-19.7M (9M actual $70.3M = Q1 $17.6M + Q2 $22.2M + Q3 $30.495M, against a $85-90M full-year guide) and Q4 revenue of $222-247M versus Q3's $251.9M actual - i.e. a sequential revenue decline and a 4-5pp margin collapse - even though census rose to ~8,050, Colorado/state Medicaid rates are fixed through 30 June, Medicare risk scores are fixed for the calendar year, and the in-house pharmacy saving is structural; the identical structure in FY2025 (9M EBITDA $23.1M vs a $24-31M guide, implying Q4 of $0.9-7.9M) produced an actual Q4 of $11.3M and a full year of $34.5M, 11% above the top of guidance.
findings.why_not_priced: Only two-to-three analysts cover the name and their numbers are visibly anchored to the guidance, not to the arithmetic: stockanalysis.com shows FY2026 consensus revenue of $966.07M last updated 2026-08-21, which backs into a Q4 revenue of $238.3M, a 5.4% sequential DECLINE from Q3, and the calendar's two Q4 EPS estimates of $0.09 are consistent with a ~$18-20M EBITDA quarter. No sell-side note, article or transcript question has laid out the implied Q4 step-down - the Q3 call transcript records that no analyst pressed management on it and management declined to forecast Q4. If the market had done this arithmetic the stock would not be drifting -5.96% over 20 days into the print at exactly the $10 average analyst target; it would be marked up toward the $13 KeyBanc target set 2026-08-21.
findings.independence: Nine-month revenue of $727.8M is confirmed independently in the 10-Q at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1834376/000183437626000022/innv-20260331.htm (filed 2026-05-08), and the Q1 FY26 $17.6M adjusted EBITDA anchor comes from a separate release at https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/11/04/3180867/0/en/InnovAge-Announces-Financial-Results-for-the-Fiscal-First-Quarter-Ended-September-30-2025.html (2025-11-04). The FY2025 precedent guide of $24-31M is from a different document again, https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/05/06/3075531/0/en/InnovAge-Announces-Financial-Results-for-the-Fiscal-Third-Quarter-Ended-March-31-2025.html (2025-05-06). Note the Q3 FY26 8-K exhibit and the Q3 FY26 call transcript are one source cluster with finding 2 - the transcript is supporting colour there, not independent evidence.

findings.finding: Colorado - InnovAge's home and largest state - enacted roughly $270M of Medicaid reimbursement cuts for FY2026-27, taking most fee-for-service rates down to 85% of Medicare from 2026-04-01 and layering a further 2.0% across-the-board reduction on HCBS waiver services for dates of service from 2026-07-01, published in the June 2026 provider bulletin after InnovAge last spoke to investors; PACE Medicaid capitation is set beneath an upper payment limit derived from exactly those FFS/HCBS costs, so the FY2027 Colorado rate InnovAge must build its first FY2027 guide around is flat-to-down rather than the mid-single-digit increases of prior years.
findings.why_not_priced: The qualitative warning IS on the wire - the CFO said on 2026-05-06 that FY2027 Medicaid increases 'may be lower than what we have experienced historically' and the CEO guided Medicare to +1.5-2%. What is not on the wire is the mechanism or the size: no published note quantifies the 85%-of-Medicare reset or the 2% July-1 HCBS cut, and the July-1 piece was only confirmed in a state provider bulletin issued a month after InnovAge's last communication. If this were priced you would see a published FY2027 EBITDA estimate cut or a downgrade in the four months since the Q3 call; instead the only rated action on file is KeyBanc reiterating Buy with a $13 target on 2026-08-21 and the stock sits at the $10 average target.
findings.independence: Independently corroborated by state budget reporting: https://www.cpr.org/2026/04/01/colorado-budget-draft-billion-shortfall-2026/ (2026-04-01, on the ~$1.5bn shortfall and the Medicaid-led cuts) and https://www.vaildaily.com/news/colorado-new-budget-cuts-medicaid/ on the signed budget. Directionally consistent with, but sourced separately from, management's own May commentary in https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/06/innovage-innv-q3-2026-earnings-transcript/ - that transcript is shared colour with finding 1 and should be collapsed to one source.

findings.finding: TCO Group Holdings (Apax and Welsh Carson) registered 112,988,070 shares - 83.2% of the 135,736,393 outstanding - for resale on a Form S-3 filed 2026-07-31 and declared effective 2026-08-05, routed there via a confidential draft registration statement submitted 2026-07-17, with no 8-K and no press release at any point; the company then scheduled FY2026 results for 2026-09-08 after the close and a Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference presentation at 08:00 ET on 2026-09-09, which is the standard sequencing for a marketed block in the window immediately after the print, and the shelf removes the Rule 144 affiliate volume cap of roughly 1.36M shares per quarter that has been the only constraint on the sponsors selling.
findings.why_not_priced: The company never announced it - InnovAge's press-release feed runs straight from 'Jennifer Browne appointed President and COO' on 2026-05-12 to the earnings-date notice on 2026-08-26 with nothing in between, and there is no 8-K. Coverage is limited to automated SEC-filing bots. The hedging evidence is decisive: the front-expiry chain carries total open interest of 15 contracts and a put/call open-interest ratio of 0.07, so essentially nobody has bought downside protection ahead of a print that could be immediately followed by a block worth many multiples of the 175,589-share average daily volume. If a secondary overhang were priced there would be visible put demand and a negative 25-delta skew; there is no chain at all.
findings.independence: The confidential draft is a second document under the same cluster (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1834376/000110465926084593/filename1.htm, submitted 2026-07-17) and I count it as one finding, not two. Genuinely separate corroboration of the back-to-back print-plus-conference calendar: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/26/3351255/0/en/innovage-announces-conference-call-to-discuss-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2026-financial-results-and-participation-in-upcoming-wells-fargo-healthcare-conference.html (2026-08-26). Cutting the other way, the July Form 4 cluster shows only RSU grants and no insider sales - CEO Patrick Blair took 78,397 RSUs on 2026-07-27 and holds 751,047 shares (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1834376/000189646326000006/xslF345X06/wk-form4_1785189578.xml), so individual insiders are not selling into strength.

searched_and_found_nothing: CMS and state PACE enrolment sanctions or audit postings current in 2026 - everything located dates to the 2021-2023 sanction cycle that was lifted, nothing new
A pre-published Wells Fargo Healthcare Conference deck on investor.innovage.com - the IR press-release page returned 503 repeatedly and no 8-K Item 7.01 deck has been furnished since 2026-05-18
New market or de novo announcements since May 2026 - the 'InnovAge to bring PACE to Terre Haute, Indiana' page that search served as current is dated 2021-11-11 and is a dead lead
Insider selling into the 157%-off-the-low move - the entire July 2026 Form 4 cluster is annual RSU grants, no open-market sales
Published sell-side or retail analysis of the implied-Q4 arithmetic - none exists; the one recent Seeking Alpha piece is a valuation-versus-price-target argument

A disclosed one-off, retroactive rate true-up or IBNR release explaining Q3's 12.1% margin - the 10-Q and the release contain no such item, and management attributed it to Medicaid rates, Medicare risk scores and in-house pharmacy
Whether Colorado's 2% ATB reduction explicitly names PACE capitation as in or out of scope - HCPF PDFs return 403 and the exemption list in Q8 of the rate-reduction Q&A could not be read
FY2027 sell-side revenue and EBITDA consensus - paywalled on every source reached, so the size of the guidance-versus-consensus gap on the forward year is unmeasured
Any news, 8-K or filing between 2026-08-26 and today that would explain the -5.09% five-day drift into the print
baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with - the chain is 15 contracts of open interest and unusable - so my only read on what is priced is the -5.96% twenty-day drift, and my main finding cuts against it while my other two are consistent with it; the honest problem is that the drift and the effective 83% resale shelf may be the same fact, in which case finding 3 is already in the tape and my positive net number is too small a residual to defend with confidence, which is why I have kept it at +2.0 against a 9.08% median historical reaction rather than sizing it to the beat I actually expect.
